subject: Capacity forecasting vs bench results — proposal and next steps
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@acme.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Sizing input for Dedicated commit — bench excerpts

Tessa —

Thanks for the quick intro call this morning. We ran a handful of questions by the infra team and they asked for concrete bench numbers and a suggested pool size. Key constraints from our side:
- Target P95 latency under 250ms for short-chat (<=256 tokens) at steady-state QPS of ~300 TPS for our assistant endpoint.
- Peak burst allowance up to ~1.5x baseline for 10 minutes.
- Multi-tenant isolation is preferred (we can accept reserved pool).

Can you share the bench excerpts you mentioned so we can align on commit sizing and an initial pricing structure? If possible, please call out headroom assumptions.

Samir Rao
Director of Platform Engineering
Acme AI

Attachments: none
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir@acme.ai>
Cc: Rachel Torres <rachel.torres@acme.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T12:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sizing input for Dedicated commit — bench excerpts

Samir —

Appreciate the specificity. I attached a short TPS / latency summary (acme_tps_summary_20261114.pdf) and a small sample of traces for the 1:1 prompt profile you described. High level takeaways:
- Measured steady-state at 300 TPS across a 64-GPU pool (8 nodes x 8-GPU equivalent config) gives median latency ~120ms, P95 ~220ms for 256-token requests using the recommended model variant and quantization profile.
- We observed burst headroom up to ~1.6x before queuing increased P95 above 350ms; adding a modest buffer (1.25x headroom) keeps P95 ~250ms.
- Prefix caching for repeated assistant prompts lowers token costs ~12% on typical workloads.

If you want, we'll run a short focused load test against your sample trace to validate identical tails. Next steps from our side: provide a pricing sketch for 12/24-month commit tiers and recommended pool packaging (preferred: 64-GPU pool with optional burst credits).

I've looped in Vivek and Marcus from Pricing + Product so we can map the bench to a commercial offer.

—Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Email: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: acme_tps_summary_20261114.pdf, trace_samples_20261114.zip

Date: 2026-11-15T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Sizing input for Dedicated commit — bench excerpts

Team — forwarding Samir's ask and the bench PDF. Quick ask: can you help convert the bench to a recommended commit + SLA construct we can send back to Acme? Specific items to price/outcome:
1) Base pool: 64-GPU reserved pool (described above).
2) Throughput guarantee: sustain 300 TPS at P95 <250ms; define acceptable slack and remediation (burst credits / auto-burst to shared capacity).
3) Headroom option: +25% burst credits for short bursts (10–15 minutes) — how to quantify monthly consumption and price?
4) Discount schedule: recommended discount for 12-mo vs 24-mo vs multi-year.
5) Credit for prefix caching and small-token reductions (optional pass-through).

I've included the sample traces. If you need a short replay against our staging cluster, we can schedule for Wednesday. Prefer an internal decision and a proposal we can send by Thursday EOD.

Thanks — Tessa

Tessa / team —

Thanks for the context. I ran the attached quick model (notes inline):
- 64-GPU pool (8 x 8-GPU boxes equivalent) is the right starting point for sustained 300 TPS with our optimized kernels and the quantized variant.
- To guarantee P95 <250ms we should include an SLA clause that allows for two short violations per quarter before remediation credits — otherwise the risk to the business is high. Suggest SLA = 99.9% for latency objective.
- Pricing suggestion: 12-month commit: list price equivalent to $X / GPU-hour with a 15% commit discount and 5% early-payment incentive; 24-month: 22% discount + 7% early pay. For strategic customers we can include an additional one-off onboarding credit.
- Burst scheme: allocate 25% burst credits (consumable minutes at baseline throughput), sold as a monthly add-on at a 40% premium to committed unit price. That preserves our capacity planning while giving Acme the short-term spikes they asked for.

I'll attach a short workbook (redwood_pricing_workbook_draft.xlsx) with an example cost table and baseline assumptions. If Marcus can map to cost-of-goods we can firm the numbers next.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Sizing input for Dedicated commit — bench excerpts

Quick comments from Product Economics:
- Confirmed: 64 GPUs is a defensible baseline. Break-even modeled at ~42% utilization of the pool given Acme's traffic shape (rely on prefix caching and batching to improve economics).
- Packaging alternative: offer a 48-GPU reserved pool + a paid buffer (auto-burst to shared capacity) that effectively buys them the same P95 during normal hours but reduces their committed spend by ~18%. This could be attractive if procurement pushes back on full 64-GPU commit.
- Recommend two commercial options in the proposal:
   A) 64-GPU reserved pool, 12-mo commit, 15% discount, 25% burst credits add-on (recommended for predictable performance)
   B) 48-GPU reserved pool, 12-mo commit, 10% discount + auto-burst buffer (lower up-front)
- Also propose a 30% onboarding credit to smooth transition costs (one-time).

I'll drop the COGS table into the workbook and flag the margin impact. If Sales wants a firmer price point for the spreadsheet to send to Acme, I'll put a conservative ratecard in tonight.

Marcus Lin
Director, Product Economics
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Sizing input for Dedicated commit — consolidated proposal

Samir / Rachel —

Thanks for your patience. Based on the bench and internal modeling, attached is a concise proposal and two packaging options:
- Option A (recommended): 64-GPU reserved pool, 12-month commit, 15% commit discount, 25% monthly burst credits (prepaid add-on), SLA: latency P95 <250ms target with 99.9% uptime/latency objective and remediation credits for repeated violations. One-time onboarding credit: 30%.
- Option B (cost-first): 48-GPU reserved pool, 12-month commit, 10% discount, auto-burst to shared capacity for short spikes, lower committed spend (est ~18% lower monthly).

Next steps if you want to proceed:
1) Confirm preferred option and any legal contacts for a standard Dedicated addendum.
2) We can schedule a 2-hour replay test next Tue (11/23) to validate tails on your real traces — we'll provide the staging endpoint and a short script.
3) Once option is selected, we provide a draft PO terms sheet and SOW; typical PO window for onboarding is 30–60 days.

Link to proposal: https://drive.redwood.com/s/ACME/bench-20261114 (sheet: redwood_dedicated_proposal_64gpu_20261118.xlsx)

If you'd like, I can also ask our Solutions team to prepare a short capacity-forecast visualization that overlays your daytime/weekend traffic patterns onto the two options so procurement can see expected consumption and margin.

Would love to get a quick signal this week.

Best —
